title: Homily LXXII
subtitle: Matthew 23:1-3
author: chrysostom
excerpt: Then. When? When He had said these things, when He had stopped their mouths; when He had brought them that they should no more dare to tempt Him; when He had…

footnotes.1: [The Greek text in this clause differs somewhat both from the received and from that followed in the R.V.—R.]
footnotes.2: [κυρου κα κυρου, referring to the two uses of the word in the Old Testament passage cited in Matt. xxii. 44, but not in precise terms.—R.]
footnotes.4: Matt. xxiii. 4. [“For,” as in rec. text.]
footnotes.7: Deut. vi. 8; so LXX. A.V. “as frontlets between.”
footnotes.8: Numb. xv. 38, 39. [The passage is freely given from the LXX.]
footnotes.10: [With the oldest New Testament mss. the word “Rabbi” is not repeated.—R.]
footnotes.11: This passage has afforded grounds for a conjecture as to the date of the Homily, but the language is too general to prove anything; see Montfaucon’s Preface.
footnotes.15: Matt. xxiii. 10. [The word καθηγητς is rendered “Master” in our English versions, but “guide” is more literal; “the Christ” (R.V.), is preferable, especially in view of the context here.—R.]
footnotes.17: Matt. xxiii. 11, 12. [R.V., “humbled,” and “humble.” The A.V. here uses both “abase” and “humble.”—R.]
footnotes.19: Or, “courts.” [στρατοπδοι; in earlier Greek “camps,” but in Byzantine Greek applied to the suite of the Emperor.—R.]
